l.i: 1. De fine peregrinationis diu multumq; cogitato, & pruden-
tium quoque amicorum consilio hac in parte utere.
2. Inperegrinando diligens & intelligens esto.
3. Tum demum ad peregrinandum appelle animum, quando
iecisti fundamenta solida doctrina; & tam diu emaneto,
donec fructum & scopum peregrinationis tuæ sis assecutus[?].
4. In diario notato quæ inter peregrinandum occurrunt insi-
gniora.
5. Doctum & pium peregrinationis socium delige.
6. Accurate dispice, quanam tibi adeunda sint loca: & par-
tim ex doctis viris atq; amicis, partim ex libris geographicis
cognosce, quid in hoc vel illo loco sit imprimis obseruandum.
7. Illorum amicitiam & beneuolentiam tibi concilia, qui à
ra-rà eruditione commendantur[?].
8. Peregrinatio literata, sit vel grammatica, sive philologica,
h.e. linguarum exoticarum causâ suscipiatur: vel topica,
h.e. cognoscendorum locorum causâ instituatur: vel ethi-
ca, i.e. morum causâ perficiatur: vel pragmatica, h.e. susci-
piatur rerum ipsarum causâ, quæ in singulis locis raræ vi-

main_text.l: su auditue reperiuntur. Peregrinatio valetudinaria, mi-
litaris, & religiosa non conuenit literarum studiolo, quâ

l.i: Et hactenus quidem vidimus ea, quæ quatuor facultatibus sunt
communia: deinceps singulas perfequemur, quatenus quidem
in Iacris[?] literis ipsarum vestigia occurrunt.

main_text.l: I. PHilosophia est vera, vel falsa. Hæc distinctio

page.notes: Printed line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 stand in the left margin and are given as notes. The printed figures at 25 and 30 sit beside lines whose text is partly obscured. Doubtful readings: "assecutus" (ink is faint), "rà" at the line break of item 7, "Iacris" (the initial may be a damaged S), and "vtere". The word "conuenit" has an odd glyph in the print and was read as conuenit. "Inperegrinando" is printed without a space. "da eft" and "fit" were corrected to est and sit per the long-s rule. The initial P of "Philosophia" is a woodcut letter. The heading "VI." is a bare number and is set as a paragraph.
